Summary: The Alternative Bank Limited has appointed Gul Khan as its Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer. The appointment followed approval from the Central Bank of Nigeria. The article text is truncated, so further details are not available.

Summary: The Federal Government has made the National Identification Number (NIN) mandatory for passengers on domestic flights. The announcement was reported by The Guardian Nigeria. The article text provides no further detail on implementation or scope.

Summary: NIPCO and NNPC have announced a new pipeline intended to supply cheaper energy to factories in Ogun State. The development is an infrastructure investment rather than a change in corporate ownership.

Entities: Bureau of Public Procurement; Director-General, Bureau of Public Procurement
Summary: The Director-General of the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP) championed a Nigeria First Procurement Agenda at the B20 USA event in Washington. The report covers his advocacy for prioritising Nigerian businesses in public procurement.

Headline: How little-known agro stock Zichis surged over 700%, crashed, and attracted a major investor
Summary: Zichis Agro-Allied Industries Plc joined the Nigerian Exchange in January 2026 with a market value of N1.09 billion. The stock later surged over 700%, then crashed, and attracted a major investor, according to Nairametrics.

Headline: NNPC probes Lagos filling station fire that destroyed seven classrooms
Summary: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) is investigating a fire at a Lagos filling station that destroyed seven classrooms. The blaze also destroyed three fuel dispensing pumps, a DAF truck and a Toyota Camry, and damaged electrical appliances in the affected classrooms.

Headline: 17 MDAs fail FG’s benchmark in 2026 Fiscal Responsibility Index
Summary: Seventeen Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) failed to meet the federal government's benchmark in the 2026 Fiscal Responsibility Index. The article headline reports the shortfall but the available text does not name the agencies or give scores.

Headline: NGX Group buys 10% ownership in Nairobi Securities Exchange to extend East African presence
Summary: NGX Group has acquired a 10% ownership stake in the Nairobi Securities Exchange, extending its presence in East Africa. The transaction was reported by Premium Times Nigeria.

Headline: $750m PIIP: Don’t gamble with retirees’ future
Entities: Pension Industry Infrastructure Platform; PenCom; FSD Africa; Chapel Hill Denham; InfraCredit
Summary: Nigeria's proposed $750 million Pension Industry Infrastructure Platform (PIIP) would mobilise about $600 million from Nigerian pension funds and at least $150 million from development finance institutions to finance infrastructure. It says an initial $350 million is expected by 2027.

Headline: Billionaire Tony Elumelu adds N98 billion stake in Seplat
Entities: Heirs Energies; Heirs Holdings; Seplat Energy Plc; Maurel & Prom; African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank); Africa Finance Corporation (AFC); Effiong Okon; Udoma Udo Udoma
Summary: Heirs Energies, the energy investment company of Tony Elumelu, bought an additional 5,888,341 Seplat Energy Plc shares at a cost of approximately N98 billion. The purchase lifts the Heirs Holdings Group's stake in Seplat to 22.05%, a holding the article values at approximately US$1.6 billion. Elumelu is also set to become Seplat's chairman effective January 1, 2027.

Headline: Sunbeth completes N19.5 billion acquisition of UAC’s 73.29% stake in Livestock Feeds, reconstitutes Board
Entities: Livestock Feeds Plc; Sunbeth Treenuts and Sesame Limited; UAC of Nigeria Plc; Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission; Securities and Exchange Commission; Nigerian Exchange Limited; Adebolanle Badejo; Temitope Omodele; Chiamaka N. Summary: Sunbeth Treenuts and Sesame Limited has completed its N19.5 billion all-cash acquisition of UAC of Nigeria Plc's 73.29% stake in Livestock Feeds Plc. The transaction followed approvals from the FCCPC, SEC and NGX, and the company has reconstituted its board with three resignations and five new directors.

Headline: Benue varsity, students bicker over staff audit, mass demotion
Summary: A dispute has emerged at a Benue State university between management, staff and students over a staff audit and a mass demotion.

Headline: GIW storms DMO, demands records on ₦88.6trn debt issuance
Summary: Global Integrity Watch (GIW) reportedly visited the Debt Management Office (DMO) and demanded records relating to ₦88.6 trillion in debt issuance.

Headline: Reps panel gives NSCDC boss 24 hours to explain alleged abuse by mining marshals
Entities: Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps
Summary: A House of Representatives panel has given the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) 24 hours to explain alleged abuse by mining marshals. The reported matter concerns conduct of NSCDC personnel deployed as mining marshals.

Headline: SPECIAL REPORT: Kano’s CNG buses remain off roads seven months after launch
Summary: Kano State's compressed natural gas (CNG) buses remain off the roads seven months after their launch, according to a Premium Times special report. The article's headline indicates the service has not yet become operational despite the launch.

Headline: Reps give NSCDC boss 24 hours over alleged N2b transactions
Entities: Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps; NSCDC Commandant-General
Summary: The House of Representatives has given the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) boss 24 hours to respond to alleged N2 billion transactions.

Headline: Elumelu ups Seplat stake to 22% with new $70 million share purchase – Report
Summary: Tony Elumelu has increased his stake in Seplat Energy to 22% through a new share purchase worth $70 million, according to a report. The transaction changes the level of significant control held by an individual in one of Nigeria's major listed oil producers.

Headline: Lasaco Assurance gets one-year extension to meet NGX free float requirement
Entities: Lasaco Assurance Plc; NGX RegCo; Gertrude Olutekunbi
Summary: Lasaco Assurance Plc has secured a one‑year extension from NGX RegCo to meet the exchange’s free float requirement, giving the insurer until 2 November 2027 to bring its free float to the mandated 20% of issued shares or a N20 billion market cap. The extension follows a sharp reduction in accumulated losses, but the firm still faces a negative retained earnings balance at the parent level.

Headline: Zamfara among eight states that fully cleared inherited pension backlogs
Entities: National Pension Commission; Zamfara State Government
Summary: On 10 November 2026 PenCom announced that Zamfara State had fully met its inherited pension obligations, joining seven other states that cleared similar backlogs. Governor Dauda Lawal credited President Tinubu’s fiscal reforms for the state’s improved capacity to settle retirees’ dues.

Headline: UNIJOS becomes Nigeria’s first university with all-female principal leadership
Summary: UNIJOS has appointed an all‑female leadership body, becoming the first university in Nigeria led entirely by women. The move marks a milestone for gender representation in the country’s higher‑education sector.

Headline: NCAA upgrades Anambra airport fire-fighting facility to Category 7 – Official
Entities: Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority; Anambra Airport
Summary: The Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority upgraded the fire‑fighting facility at Anambra Airport to Category 7, meeting higher safety standards for aviation operations. The upgrade follows formal regulatory procedures and is mandatory for airports hosting larger aircraft. The move is expected to enhance safety compliance on Nigerian air transport routes.

Headline: UniAbuja land cut approved by Wike’s predecessor – FCTA
Entities: Federal Capital Territory Administration; University of Abuja
Summary: Under the Federal Capital Territory Administration, a land cut was approved for the University of Abuja. The decision was made by Wike’s predecessor, David Mark. This allocation will facilitate the university’s expansion within the Abuja city limits.

Headline: FG dismisses alleged irregularities in livestock ministry HQ deal amid procurement questions
Entities: Federal Ministry of Livestock Development; Osas & Oseji Estate Surveyors & Valuers
Summary: The Federal Ministry of Livestock Development denied allegations of irregularities in the purchase of its Abuja headquarters. The ministry confirmed that the N8.94 billion payment to Osas & Oseji Estate Surveyors & Valuers on 17 September 2025 complied with government approval and procurement procedures and that the acquisition was necessary for its nascent operations.

Headline: NGX Group acquires 10% strategic stake in Nairobi Securities Exchange
Entities: NGX Group Plc; Nairobi Securities Exchange
Summary: NGX Group Plc has acquired a 10% equity stake in Nairobi Securities Exchange, expanding its investment footprint in East Africa as part of its pan‑African growth strategy.

Headline: Form 4 Ibotta Inc: KDT Ibotta Holdings, LLC (10% Owner) For: 9 November
Entities: Ibotta Inc; KDT Ibotta Holdings, LLC
Summary: KDT Ibotta Holdings, LLC disclosed a 10% ownership stake in Ibotta Inc on 9 November, as reported in a Form 4 filing. The disclosure signals a significant level of control that surpasses Nigeria’s 5% threshold for Persons with Significant Control.

Headline: NNPC showcases methane reduction progress at COP31
Summary: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) showcased its methane reduction progress at COP31, the UN climate conference. The article text provided is limited to the headline, so no further details are available.

Headline: “Wealth Of Experience And Expertise” — MTN Nigeria Names Prof. Fabian Ajogwu, SAN, Among Five New Board Directors
Summary: MTN Nigeria has appointed Prof. Fabian Ajogwu, SAN, as one of five new board directors. The announcement was reported by TheNigeriaLawyer under the headline citing the company's "wealth of experience and expertise".

Headline: Customs, EFCC join forces against smuggling, money laundering
Entities: Nigeria Customs Service, Sokoto/Zamfara Area Command; Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC); Haliru Abdullahi; Nwanneka Nwonkike; Bashir Tanimu
Summary: The Nigeria Customs Service Sokoto/Zamfara Area Command and the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission have pledged to strengthen collaboration against smuggling, money laundering and other economic and financial crimes. The commitment followed a courtesy visit by Customs Area Controller DC Haliru Abdullahi to the EFCC Sokoto Zonal Directorate. The agencies agreed to share intelligence, exchange information and coordinate enforcement operations.

Headline: Taskforce seals pharmaceutical company in Kano
Summary: A taskforce sealed a pharmaceutical company in Kano, according to a Guardian Nigeria report.

Headline: UK buys £1bn Nigerian oil as Dangote refinery expands
Summary: The United Kingdom has purchased £1 billion worth of Nigerian oil as the Dangote refinery expands. The transaction underscores continued international demand for Nigerian crude and signals investment in the country’s refining capacity.

Headline: FCCPC seals real estate firm over alleged failure to deliver N140 million home
Entities: Peachville Platinum Estate Limited; Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission
Summary: FCCPC seized Peachville Platinum Estate Limited for allegedly failing to deliver a N140 million property in Abuja after a consumer complaint. The governing body issued a compliance notice on 17 August 2026, but the company did not comply by the deadline and was consequently sealed. The enforcement highlights the Commission’s willingness to act against non‑compliant developers.

Headline: Sunrisal gets $25,000 ECOWAS grant for rural solar
Summary: Sunrisal secured a $25,000 grant from ECOWAS to support rural solar initiatives. The funding is earmarked to expand renewable energy access in ECOWAS member states.

Headline: US firm to build $100m Bayelsa gas processing plant
Entities: Bayelsa State Government; Fulcrum LNG Incorporated; Westpaq International
Summary: Bayelsa State Government announced a partnership with U.S.-based Fulcrum LNG Inc. to construct a multi‑million‑dollar gas gathering and processing plant that will capture flared gas and supply power to the state’s Independent Power Plant. The project was agreed at the US‑Nigeria Governors G2B Forum in Sugar Land, Texas, with a planned investment of about US $100 million.

Headline: Tinubu breaks ground for $3.5bn Bakassi Deep Seaport
Entities: Bakassi Deep Seaport; Government of Nigeria
Summary: President Bola Tinubu inaugurated the construction of the Bakassi Deep Seaport, a $3.5 billion maritime project intended to bolster trade and create jobs in Nigeria’s south‑coast region. The ground‑breaking marks a significant step in the country’s infrastructure development agenda.

Headline: Rivers gas seepage puts 13 oil wells in high-risk category, NUPRC finds
Summary: The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission screened 28 oil and gas wells near reported gas seepage sites in Bille Community, Degema Local Government Area, Rivers State, and identified 13 wells as high or very high risk.

Headline: FG opens 3MTT Cohort 5 applications, secures N4b funding
Summary: The Federal Government has opened applications for the third‑generation 3MTT Cohort 5 talent development programme and secured N4 billion in funding to support the initiative.

Headline: NIMASA, China deepen maritime cooperation
Summary: NIMASA and China Maritime Safety Administration signed a Memorandum of Understanding to deepen maritime cooperation, covering safety training, crew safety, and technology exchange.

Headline: FG seals Abuja estate over alleged rights violations
Summary: The Federal Government sealed an Abuja estate after alleged violations of residents’ rights. The move was aimed at enforcing land‑use regulations and stopping further infringement.

Headline: UNIJOS appoints first female vice-chancellor, Patricia Lar
Summary: Patricia Lar has been appointed as the first female vice‑chancellor of UNIJOS, marking a milestone in the university’s leadership.

Headline: Bayelsa announces US gas plant deal, but investment value remains uncertain
Summary: Bayelsa State government announced the initiation of a gas plant project with a United States partner, though the investment amount and specific contractor have not been disclosed.

Headline: ICPC recovers N5.3b from LG accounts, to post councils’ books online
Summary: ICPC has recovered N5.3 billion from local government accounts and will publish the council books online, enhancing financial transparency. The move signals a push to curb misappropriations at the LG level. The recovered funds will be made publicly available for scrutiny.

Headline: NMDPRA moves to curb tanker crashes, sensitises drivers
Summary: NMDPRA announced a new initiative to curb tanker crashes by sensitising drivers on safety procedures. The agency aims to reduce incidents involving petroleum tanker transport.

Headline: Lagos plans procurement reforms beyond Sanwo-Olu
Summary: Lagos State announced plans to extend procurement reforms beyond the tenure of former Governor Sanwo-Olu, signalling a new commitment to transparency in public spending.

Headline: Ngige: Witness tells court of presidential directives on NSITF contracts
Summary: Witness in Ngige court testified about presidential directives governing contracts of the National Social Insurance Trust Fund. The hearing underscored the executive branch’s oversight role in NSITF’s procurement processes.

Headline: NCC’s device registration policy could hike phone prices, expert warns
Summary: The Nigeria Communications Commission announced a new device registration policy that could raise the retail price of mobile phones, according to an expert warning.

Headline: Afreximbank acquires stake in D’banj’s CREAM platform
Entities: Afreximbank; CANEX Creations Incorporated; CREAM; D’Kings Men Media Ltd
Summary: The African Export‑Import Bank, through its vehicle CANEX Creations Incorporated, has acquired an equity stake in CREAM, the AI‑powered creative platform founded by Nigerian singer D’banj. The deal, formalised on 6 November 2026, is part of the bank’s $2 billion commitment to Africa’s creative sector and aims to boost commercial value and intellectual‑property retention for creatives.

Headline: EFCC secures conviction of mining firm, two others in Kwara
Summary: EFCC secured convictions of a mining firm and two other entities in Kwara following a regulatory probe. The action underscores the Commission's commitment to enforcing mining laws within the state.

Headline: Emefiele acquired properties through proxies, EFCC tells court
Summary: The Enforcement and Financial Crimes Commission, in a Nigerian court hearing, alleged that former Central Bank governor Chukwuma Emefiele acquired properties through proxies. The claim is part of an ongoing probe into potential misuse of office, raising questions about transparency and legality.

Headline: BII backs Okra with $7m to accelerate clean energy
Entities: British International Investment; Okra; Rural Electrification Agency; Jonny Baxter; Geoffrey Manley; Afnan Hannan
Summary: British International Investment (BII) announced a $7m debt facility to Okra, a mesh-grid technology provider for off-grid communities. The financing is intended to fund equipment procurement for approximately 150,000 new connections, primarily in Nigeria. The facility is expected to shorten equipment delivery to Nigeria from four months to about two months.

Headline: Lagos clamps down on ‘no refund’ store rules
Summary: Lagos State has moved to crack down on retail stores that enforce 'no refund' policies. The article text provided is limited to the headline, so further details on the enforcement measures are not available.

Headline: Weak oversight, market gaps stall power tariff reforms
Summary: Power tariff reforms in Nigeria are reported to be stalled by weak regulatory oversight and market gaps. The article's text is limited to its headline, so no further details on the parties, figures or timelines are available.

Headline: Senate summons NCC, MTN, Airtel, others over poor network, unjustified airtime deductions
Entities: Nigerian Communications Commission; MTN Nigeria; Airtel Nigeria; Globacom; T2; Ikra Bilbis; Tahir Monguno; Lola Ashiru; Ned Nwoko
Summary: The Nigerian Senate has summoned the Nigerian Communications Commission and major telecom operators, including MTN, Airtel, Globacom and T2, over persistent network failures and alleged unjustified airtime deductions. A Senate Committee on Communications, chaired by Ikra Bilbis, has been mandated to investigate subscriber losses and report back within four weeks. The resolution followed a motion on consumer protection sponsored by Tahir Monguno and presented by Lola Ashiru.

Headline: EFCC re-arraigns ex-Skye Bank chair Tunde Ayeni on N15.6bn fraud charges
Entities: Skye Bank; Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC); Tunde Ayeni
Summary: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has re-arraigned Tunde Ayeni, a former chairman of Skye Bank, on fraud charges totalling N15.6bn. The re-arraignment concerns alleged fraud linked to a former bank chair, a matter of corporate governance accountability in Nigeria's banking sector.

Headline: UK backs Nigeria’s proposed $750m pension infrastructure fund
Summary: The United Kingdom has backed Nigeria's proposed $750 million pension infrastructure fund.

Headline: Afreximbank, DBN partner on $75 million finance facility for SMEs, creative sector
Summary: Afreximbank and the Development Bank of Nigeria (DBN) have partnered on a $75 million finance facility aimed at small and medium-sized enterprises and the creative sector. The announcement was reported by Premium Times Nigeria. No further details on terms or timelines are provided in the available text.

Headline: Minister suspends broadcast licence fee reviews, urges highest standard ahead 2027 elections
Summary: The Minister has suspended reviews of broadcast licence fees and urged broadcasters to maintain the highest standards ahead of the 2027 elections. The directive was reported by The Guardian Nigeria.

Headline: FG moves to regulate scrap metal industry, curb infrastructure vandalism
Summary: The Federal Government has moved to regulate the scrap metal industry in an effort to curb infrastructure vandalism.
